angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 640,044 km at 139.76 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.1550 +/- 0.0161 mas (same row, RUWE 0.96): 139.76 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.92 +/- 0.034 solar radii from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-265 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract): 640,044 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.901 +/- 0.051 solar masses from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-265 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5420 +/- 100 K from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-265 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-265 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-265.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.465, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
